texts: Materials in quarantine cannot be issued to production.
Released materials are moved to the approved area promptly.
The warehouse clerk scans the container label before issuing material; an unreleased container is refused.
Expired materials should be blocked automatically.
Material status is changed from quarantine to released.
QA changes the material status from quarantine to released with an e-signature.
Retest dates are calculated from the date of receipt using the retest interval in the material master.
Stock levels must be accurate.
Instruments that are overdue for calibration cannot be selected in a batch step.
Calibration certificates are uploaded and approved.
The metrology engineer approves each calibration certificate before the instrument returns to use.
Calibration intervals can be extended by the engineer.
A calibration interval can be extended once, by up to 30 days, with a documented justification approved by QA.
Preventive maintenance is scheduled at suitable intervals.
It is flagged on the equipment dashboard when maintenance is overdue.
Maintenance work orders are closed by the technician and verified by the area supervisor.
Particle counts above the alert limit trigger an alarm to the area supervisor within 1 minute.
Excursions must be investigated.
Microbiology can edit plate counts after they are entered.
Viable monitoring results are trended monthly per room and sampling point.
The trend chart should highlight unusual results.
Settle plates are exposed for no more than 4 hours.
Sampling locations are TBD per room classification.
Every complaint is logged within 1 working day of receipt.
Complaints are acknowledged to the customer quickly.
The complaint handler may close a complaint with no investigation if it is not product-related.
A complaint can be reopened by the complaint owner.
Recall decisions are documented and approved by the quality head with an e-signature.
Customers are informed of a recall within the required timeframe.
This must include the batch number and the reason for the recall.
Each saleable pack receives a unique serial number that is never reused.
Serial numbers can be decommissioned by the packaging operator.
Aggregation data is sent to the national repository without delay.
Aggregation data is sent to the national repository within 15 minutes of the case being sealed.
The line should reject packs with unreadable codes.
The vision system rejects packs whose 2D code grade is below C, and logs each rejection.
Suppliers are requalified every 3 years or after a major quality event.
New suppliers are approved before first use.
The supplier questionnaire covers quality, regulatory, logistics, etc.
A supplier can be removed from the approved list by purchasing.
Audit findings are closed within the agreed period.
The supplier scorecard is updated every quarter from delivery, complaint and audit data.
Serious adverse events are reported to the authority within 15 calendar days.
Case narratives must be clear and complete.
The safety physician signs each medical assessment electronically.
Case data can be changed after submission.
Trial master file documents are filed within 5 working days of finalisation.
Essential documents are QC-checked.
The eTMF must support all relevant document types.
Site staff might need access to the investigator folder.
Each use, cleaning and maintenance event is entered in the equipment logbook with user, date and time.
Logbook entries are reviewed by production.
A logbook entry can be deleted by the supervisor.
Swab results must be below the acceptance limit.
Swab results must be below 10 ppm of the previous product.
Cleaning must be effective.
The dirty hold time is to be defined by validation.
Equipment must be cleaned within 24 hours of batch end.
Cleaning records are verified before the equipment is released for the next batch.
The cleaning log is simple to fill in on the shop floor.
